rationale: The isolated-eugenol mouse beam results differ across schedules that lack separately matched model controls. The other reports measure exploratory behavior, rotation or abnormal movement. Ground allspice and clinical Parkinson walking slowness remain unresolved.

The Bordeaux outbreak reports dysarthria after contaminated preserved sardines. The distinct Minamata study reuses an earlier exposed cohort and reports examiner-rated dysarthria after historical exposure through unspecified seafood. The Parkinson diet data pool oily fish. A grilled-sardine and speech-intelligibility contrast remains unresolved.

A Parkinson cohort reports an association between a whole dietary score and insomnia. The MIND trial gives a whole-diet sleep-quality contrast, with bean varieties grouped. Kidney-bean yogurt data are uncontrolled. The completed boiled-pinto crossover enrolled a different population and measured other outcomes. Boiled pinto and clinical Parkinson insomnia remain unresolved.

Cinnamon has been used as an odor cue in Parkinson screening and as part of an inhaled smell-training program. The Veranópolis protocol and later public prevalence report supply no individual cinnamon result. Evidence on ingesting ground cinnamon and Parkinson olfaction remains unresolved.
